newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oil drilling to resume in UAE emirate.
newsitem.headline: Oil drilling to resume in UAE emirate.

text.p: U.S. firm Ras Al-Khaimah Oil and Gas Co Ltd will drill two exploration oil wells in the Gulf Arab emirate in the first quarter of next year, Felix Molloy, general manager of the firm said on Wednesday.
"With regard to the future of hydrocarbon potential we are optimistic," Molloy told Reuters.

There has been no commercial oil production in Ras Al-Khaimah -- one of the seven emirates that make up the oil-rich United Arab Emirates (UAE) -- since condensate output at the offshore Saleh field hit plateau in the late eighties.
The firm will complete an analysis of offshore and onshore seismic data by the end of this year and from this it will decide where to drill the wells early next year, Molloy said.
This included a 370 km (231 miles) high resolution survey of the emirate's onshore acreage.

Ras al-Khaimah, smaller than Rhode Island with a population of just over 150,000, is dwarfed in oil terms by Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Sharjah which account for UAE output of 2.2 million barrels per day (bpd).
The company is backed by Bahamas-based top U.S. investor Michael Dingman and former White House Chief of Staff John Sununu.
Though few expect major new finds in Ras al-Khaimah, higher oil prices and the Dingman-backed firm could awaken interest in this and other plays in the region which have been neglected.
U.S. firm Atlantic Richfield Co already has rights to the emirate's offshore Baih field and is looking at plans to resume production, an industry source in the UAE said.
